source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed electrical appliance safety checks

1. Start with the test records.
2.
completion:
a. Identify the appliance model, make, and serial number.
b. Record the date and time of the safety check.
c. Specify the name and qualifications of the person performing the check.

3. Document testing procedures.
a. List the standard testing procedures used in accordance with relevant safety standards (e.g., IEC, NFPA, OSHA).
b. Describe any additional tests performed, if relevant.

4. Record test results.
a. Detail each test conducted (e.g., insulation resistance test, earth continuity test, polarity check, current leakage test, etc.).
b. Note the expected results according to safety standards and compare them with actual results.
c. Describe any anomalies or failures observed during the tests.

5. Take photographs or videos where necessary.
a. Capture images of the appliance, test setup, and any observed damage or malfunctions.
b. Ensure that these visuals support the documented findings.

6. Create a detailed narrative.
